  PROBLEM: Every HTTP 403 is classified as transient, including permanent cases such as "bot was kicked from the group chat". The 403 branch was added deliberately in the last run, so this is a known trade-off and not a regression.
  WHY: If the bot permanently loses chat access, the affected tracking comments are never deleted. Each cleanup call prints a `::warning::` and makes up to 3 Telegram calls, bounded by the breaker and 10-second timeouts.

- scripts/tg_helpers.sh:235 | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The cleanup mechanism treats HTTP 403 (Forbidden) from Telegram as a transient error.
  WHY: A 403 is often permanent, for example an invalid bot token or a bot kicked from the group. Retries are bounded to 3 consecutive failures, but tracking comments can be left behind and warnings repeat on later cleanup runs until the issue is resolved manually.
